* mu. Cas.label: Mu Cas A
* mu. Cas.scope: Primary Mu Cas A, not the total mass of the binary or the faint B component. The catalog retains the existing Mu Cas system marker and motion.
* mu. Cas.note: Bond et al. 2020: primary dynamical mass (Table 7), photospheric [Fe/H] (Table 9), preferred temperature and luminosity (§9.1), and model age (§9.2). Radius is the parallax-adjusted interferometric value in Table 9. The paper suspects the interferometric angular diameter is overestimated by a few percent, and explicitly treats temperature, radius, helium content and age as uncertain. The adopted surface [Fe/H]=-0.81 differs from the initial abundance used for diffusion-inclusive stellar models. Luminosity and mass use this paper's parallax and are retained as published, not recomputed with the catalog's orbit-contaminated Gaia component parallax.

radius_solar.caveat: Formal uncertainty excludes the suspected angular-diameter systematic; see §8.1.

age_gyr.caveat: Suggestive model estimate sensitive to temperature, angular diameter, helium and element diffusion.

* rho Per.label: Rho Persei (Gorgonea Tertia)
* rho Per.note: Tables 2-3, row E: direct granulation-scaling mass and Stefan-Boltzmann radius; luminosity converts log10(L/Lsun)=3.43 +/-0.03, adopted there from McDonald et al. 2017. Published values retain their source temperature (3479 +/-125 K); the catalog's existing spectroscopic temperature and [Fe/H] remain unchanged. Mass is not an orbital/dynamical measurement; radius is not interferometric. No age is adopted because this paper reports none.

mass_solar.caveat: Empirical granulation calibration and the paper's radius; not a dynamical mass.

luminosity_solar.caveat: McDonald et al. 2017 SED value as adopted by Kallinger; retained at the publication's distance.

radius_solar.caveat: Published radius uses 3479 K, not the catalog's preserved 3619 K temperature.

G 272-61A.label: Luyten 726-8 A (GJ 65 A)
G 272-61A.scope: Individual A component, not the unresolved GJ 65 binary.
G 272-61A.note: Kervella et al. 2016 interferometric radius; MacDonald et al. 2018 resolved bolometric luminosity and temperature using that radius; GRAVITY Collaboration 2024 dynamical mass. Radii/luminosities are retained at their published parallax of 373.70 mas, while the mass uses 371.92 mas. No scalar age is adopted: the magnetic-model ages are assumptions, not age determinations.

temperature_k.caveat: Bolometric flux with BT-Settl missing-flux correction and Kervella 2016 radius; not a spectral-class temperature.

mass_solar.caveat: GRAVITY 2024 orbit and adopted parallax; not the binary total mass.

luminosity_solar.caveat: Resolved flux ratio and BT-Settl correction outside 1.0435-3.770 microns; retained at the published distance.

radius_solar.caveat: Published limb-darkened diameter and parallax, not recomputed with orbit-contaminated Gaia component parallaxes.

metallicity_dex.caveat: Component-resolved UVES spectrum fitted relative to Proxima; method-dependent abundance. Adopted consistently for both A and B from Kervella et al. (2016), with +/-0.20 dex uncertainty.

G 272-61B.label: Luyten 726-8 B (GJ 65 B)
G 272-61B.scope: Individual B component, not the unresolved GJ 65 binary.
G 272-61B.note: Kervella et al. 2016 interferometric radius; MacDonald et al. 2018 resolved bolometric luminosity and temperature using that radius; GRAVITY Collaboration 2024 dynamical mass. Radii/luminosities are retained at their published parallax of 373.70 mas, while the mass uses 371.92 mas. No scalar age is adopted: the magnetic-model ages are assumptions, not age determinations. Supersedes catalog [Fe/H]=-0.42 dex from 2023ApJS..266...41P, also reported by 2012A&A...538A.143K. Kervella et al. (2016), section 2.3, identify the older -0.42 +/-0.10 dex result as a low-resolution combined A+B spectrum, potentially biased low by rapid rotation; it is retained as historical system-level evidence, not an adopted B-component abundance.
